title: Memora Oracle ADB is unreachable — fallback procedure
keywords: memora oracle adb database down unreachable outage fallback
body: When the Memora Oracle Autonomous Database (ADB) is unreachable, Memora fails closed: the API returns an explicit error, and no local SQLite file ever becomes an authority for shared memory. Keep serving reference knowledge from the bundled offline pack, queue new writes for retry instead of inventing local state, and report the outage to Muse on hub #1483. The offline pack complements the ADB store; it never replaces it, and anything it answers is labelled offline-pack so a reader never mistakes it for live store data.

title: FRIDAY cgroup memory guard
keywords: friday oom memory cgroup guard warn critical
body: FRIDAY runs under a 200 MB cgroup cap (MemoryMax=200M, MemorySwapMax=192M); the kernel OOM-kills the process at that limit, not at system-RAM exhaustion. The merged memory guard (TASK-FRD-041) warns at 75% of the cgroup cap and goes critical at 90%, sending a direct Telegram warning with a 5-minute cooldown, and recovers below 60%. If FRIDAY dies silently, check kern.log for an OOM kill of the python process before assuming a crash bug.

title: FRIDAY voice greeting-onset latency bar
keywords: friday voice greeting onset latency 8 seconds
body: Voice is judged on speed first: the greeting-onset bar is 8 seconds from call start to FRIDAY's first spoken word. The onset defect (TASK-VOI-028) was the greeting gate's 5-second asyncio wait that could not fire while session start blocked the job loop. A calm-window re-probe is the proof: onset is measured live, not inferred from logs.

title: Stratex trades demo only
keywords: stratex trading demo live paper profit
body: Stratex trades demo only, with no live trading and no profit promises — progress is proven by the forward record on demo, never by a live fill. Any task that asks for live trading, a live brokerage connection, or a promised return is refused under the standing order. Demo fills, journals, and digests are the evidence; a backtest alone is not a result.

title: Free-only services rule
body: No paid services, tiers, or pay-as-you-go, ever. Every provider Memora, Inference, and the fleet touch must have a free tier that actually answers — APInex's free tier (15 requests per minute, no SLA) is a fallback rung by design, never a primary. If a service needs a card, a trial, or a paid key, the task stops and the block is reported instead.

title: Reporting: only message to Muse
body: Never message Surendra in this chat; every update goes to Muse, the Head Manager, on hub issue #1483 — his direct order of 2026-11-24 00:18 IST. Hub posts happen only on claim, completion-with-evidence, or blocked-with-reason; hourly 'still working' posts are abolished. Every board or issue post is signed '— Muse 2', and no secret is ever pasted anywhere because the repo is public.

title: Memora capture, compress, inject cycle
keywords: memora capture compress inject session context
body: Memora's session cycle is capture, compress, inject: every turn is captured as a session event through POST /v1/capture/events, the session compresses into a digest at session end, and the next session starts with an injected context pack from GET /v1/capture/context. Production callers for the three shipped-but-never-invoked services (skill learning, user model, session capture) landed in TASK-MEM-029. The digest promotion gate decides whether a compressed session becomes SEMANTIC memory.

title: Memora session needle taxonomy
keywords: memora needles decision bugfix security sensitive session index
body: Every captured Memora event is classified into the claude-mem needle taxonomy: decision, bugfix, security_alert, security_note, sensitive, feature, refactor, discovery, change, and observation as the fallback. Security and sensitive win on priority — a fix for a vulnerability is a security_alert, and a secret marker is sensitive. Sensitive needles never render their content in a timeline or detail read, and the L0 session index rides in the session-start pack (TASK-MEM-031).

title: Memora Obsidian vault second brain
keywords: memora obsidian vault second brain nightly summaries
body: The Obsidian-vault second brain (TASK-MEM-030) renders Memora's store as plain-Markdown notes — Inbox, Daily Logs, Projects, Areas, Resources, Memories, Archive — plus one note per agent and a root index, so the whole second brain is readable without the service running. A nightly job writes one per-agent work summary into Daily Logs from the capture-event stream. Private-scope records are excluded unless explicitly included; a personal vault must never silently publish an agent-private memory.

title: Inference fallback waterfall and APInex
keywords: inference apinex fallback groq openrouter gemini router
body: Inference routes through a free waterfall — groq, then openrouter, then gemini — with APInex as the last free rung (TASK-INF-030). APInex is OpenAI-compatible, defaults to free/qwen-3.8-max, and is rate-limited to 10 requests per minute under its 15 RPM free-tier cap. Failover was proven in staging with the primary forced down: APInex served in 3.23 seconds. Free-tier models that return a 402 billing error despite a free/ prefix are gated and must not be retried as free.

title: Project NOMAD — offline-first knowledge server
keywords: nomad offline knowledge server wikipedia ollama
body: Project NOMAD (Crosstalk-Solutions/project-nomad, Apache-2.0) is an offline-first knowledge and education server: Wikipedia, books, courses, maps, and optional local AI, all running on hardware you own with no internet required after install. A Command Center orchestrates containerized tools over Docker; the core needs about 5 GB of disk and under 1 GB of RAM, and there is zero built-in telemetry. Internet is required only during installation and when the user chooses to download more content.

title: Offline Wikipedia with Kiwix and ZIM files
keywords: kiwix zim wikipedia offline medical ebooks
body: NOMAD's Information Library serves offline Wikipedia, medical references, survival guides, and ebooks through Kiwix, which reads ZIM archive files — each ZIM is one self-contained snapshot of a whole site. A ZIM library manager and a Wikipedia content selector let the user pick exactly which snapshots to keep, so the offline library stays a curated subset instead of an unbounded download. The Memora offline pack copies this idea at small scale: a versioned manifest names the corpus subset, and the pack never fetches anything at query time.

title: Local AI with Ollama
keywords: ollama local ai llm qdrant rag
body: NOMAD's AI Assistant runs local chat with document upload and semantic search (RAG over Qdrant) on Ollama, or on any OpenAI-compatible server such as LM Studio or llama.cpp. Adding the assistant brings an install to roughly 25 GB because the model needs about its download size in memory while it answers. The Memora offline pack deliberately does not ship a model: its fallback answers come from BM25 ranking over a bundled corpus, so the pack stays dependency-light and answers with no model, no vector store, and no network.

title: Offline maps with ProtoMaps
body: NOMAD serves downloadable regional maps offline through ProtoMaps: a region's map is a single portable tile archive the device reads locally, with no tile server and no network at view time. Maps are picked per region, like the rest of NOMAD's content — the pack ships what the user chose, nothing more. The pattern the Memora pack takes from this is per-region, per-collection selection: a defined subset, declared in a manifest, instead of a mirror of everything.

title: Offline courses with Kolibri and Khan Academy
keywords: kolibri khan academy courses offline education
body: NOMAD's Education Platform runs Khan Academy courses with progress tracking through Kolibri, entirely offline and multi-user. Courses are installed as curated collections, and progress is tracked locally on the device. For Memora, the lesson is that an offline pack is a teaching corpus as much as a reference one: the pack's education collection exists so a fallback answer can also point at the course that explains it.

title: How the Memora offline pack works
keywords: offline pack memora manifest bm25 fallback switch
body: The Memora offline pack (TASK-MEM-032) is a versioned, bundled corpus subset — a manifest plus one JSONL file — that answers queries with stdlib-only BM25 ranking when the Oracle ADB path is down. The fallback switch is strict: ADB up means ADB wins, even if the pack would rank a hit higher; ADB down, empty, or unconfigured means the pack answers and says so. The pack imports nothing from Memora's store or network layers, so it still loads when the thing that is down is the import chain itself.
